doc.title: Hide Tanaka interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014

title: Dreaming of a jazz life; teenage rock guitar and electric bass in Japan
summary: Tanaka dreamed of jazz from about 16, but played rock and blues alone as a kid: B.B. King, Led Zeppelin, Grand Funk, Chicago, Blood Sweat and Tears, heard on records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well I wanted to start out — I saw something on your website that I thought was well- said. And someone was talking about you and it talked about when you finally got to New York. “He started the jazz life that he had always dreamed of.” So you had always dreamed of a jazz life?
Um hum.
From what age did you start to dream of a jazz life?

Sometime from high school, like at 16 years old. Also I started on acoustic bass. Before that I played just rock music, guitar, electric bass. My generation in Japan, mostly, 90 percent of the kids were rock kids. Not jazz at that time.
Not what?
Not jazz.
I’m glad you said that because it’s a question I wanted to ask. So you were born in 1956?
’56, yeah.
So we’re talking maybe 1970ish?
Yes, seventies.
You were playing rock music?
Yeah, just as a kid. Not with a band, so just myself. Rock, blues.
What were some of the artists that you were playing?
I liked first, B.B. King, the blues. And then, so many rock bands: Led Zeppelin. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -2-
Oh, Led Zeppelin?
Yeah Zeppelin and Grand Funk Railroad, Chicago, Blood, Sweat and Tears.
Ooh, my favorite. And how did you hear this music. Did you buy LP’s?

Yeah, yeah. Always American was English, the pop charts, just who came through Japan. Actually American hit songs and England, rock hit songs, almost at the same time in Japan they were a big hit too. Yeah.
Did you and your friends speak English at that time?
No. When I came to New York I couldn’t speak anything. Couldn’t read.
I find it really fascinating that you were listening to American rock & roll sung in English. When you played it, did you sing it in Japanese?
No, no, no, no, just I imitate the guitar. Yeah. I really don’t know about the singing.
You were just the guitar player?
Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.
Were you playing electric bass?
Yeah, sometimes electric bass yeah.
You played rock & roll guitar then.
Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.
I just find that fascinating how the world is very small now. With music it gets spread around so much.
Right.
